blockerFindings.whyThisIsABlocker: G09LJ-V4-B2 named exactly one location, $.basedOn.permissionJoinV7.review.verdict, and exactly one false string, 'Codex not reviewed'. The subject did not correct that string. It added a sibling review.codex object and a new permissionJoinV7.verdict key carrying the true standing, and left the false string in place. Three consequences follow. First, the artifact now asserts both 'Codex not reviewed' and 'Codex REJECT 0/1 PLJ-V7-SF1' about the same reviewer and the same subject inside the same object, so it is self-contradictory on a matter of fact rather than merely incomplete. Second, review.verdict is the canonical field this artifact uses for every other cited input — g09v3, namedCatalog, permissionJoinV6, predecessor, r6r10InputCorpusV2, predecessorV2 and predecessorV3 all carry their standing there and nowhere else — so a consumer reading the field consistently across basedOn reads the false value for v7 and the true value for everything else. Third, findingDisposition records G09LJ-V4-B2 as disposition ACCEPTED with landedAt 'basedOn.permissionJoinV7.review.codex', which claims a repair at a newly created key while the defect location goes untouched; the artifact therefore asserts a disposition it did not perform. A turn whose stated purpose is to land three findings cannot record one as ACCEPTED while the flagged bytes still read as they did before.
blockerFindings.materialityHonest: The true Codex standing of v7 is stated correctly in three other places in the subject, and the leftover arithmetic is unaffected. This is a correctness-of-record defect, not a measurement defect. Repair is a one-field edit.
blockerFindings.repairDirection: Set $.basedOn.permissionJoinV7.review.verdict to the true standing — for example 'Claude ACCEPT 0/0; Codex REJECT 0/1 PLJ-V7-SF1; CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED' — or restructure so the claude2 review object states only the Claude verdict and no reviewer-wide claim. Then either drop the now-redundant permissionJoinV7.verdict key or keep it as the single reviewer-wide field, but do not leave two fields making opposite factual claims. Update findingDisposition.landedAt for G09LJ-V4-B2 to name the corrected path.
blockerFindings.refutedAlternative: Considered and rejected: that review.verdict is scoped to the claude2 file it sits beside, so 'Codex not reviewed' is a statement about that file rather than about Codex. The field's own text defeats this — it says 'Claude ACCEPT 0/0; Codex not reviewed', naming both reviewers, which is why every sibling entry uses it to carry the full two-reviewer standing. It is a reviewer-wide claim in a review-wide field, and it is false.

decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.scopeOfReject: This REJECT is of g09-leftover-join.v5 as a current G09 execution-remainder remeasurement. It is not a rejection of the leftover partition, which is unchanged from frozen v3 and v4 and survives every attack, nor of the two new citations, which are correct and correctly recorded. It is a rejection of an incomplete landing: one of the three turn findings was recorded ACCEPTED while the exact string it flagged still stands, and one supporting sentence still rests on the superseded predecessor.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The subject is unmoved at d9b35579… mode 0444, and all 58 cited digests recompute byte-exactly, including the new permission-leftover-join.v9 pair, the doctor-actor-leftover-join.v11 triple, and both g09-leftover-join.v4 verdicts. Live required-now is 28 and the DR-G09 token is OPEN, both matching. The obligation set, leftoverDesign map, fourteen FX classes, R-10/R-6 race set and the entire summary object are identical to frozen v3 and v4, so the measurement was preserved while the citation layer was reworked, and frozen v4 is unmoved and correctly declined as a current remeasurement. Twenty-three of twenty-five attacks are refuted. G09-V4-SF1 is fully landed and verified: doctor-actor-leftover-join.v11 is registerRow DR-114 with OBL-FC-C1 and OBL-BLK-1..4 each leftoverDesign true, recorded by ADOPTED D-170, whose three pinned digests equal the subject's exactly, and the DR-114 remainder is named without being taken. G09LJ-V4-B1 is landed in five places, including the replacement of v7 by D-171/v9 as the current DR-105 ROW leftover-join, with v9's eight-member leftoverDesign list verified against live bytes. Two defects remain. The blocker is that G09LJ-V4-B2 is recorded as disposition ACCEPTED while $.basedOn.permissionJoinV7.review.verdict still reads 'Claude ACCEPT 0/0; Codex not reviewed; CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED' — the exact string and exact path that finding named. The turn added a sibling review.codex block and a new permissionJoinV7.verdict key carrying the true REJECT 0/1 PLJ-V7-SF1 standing but did not correct the flagged field, so the artifact now states both 'Codex not reviewed' and 'Codex REJECT 0/1' about the same reviewer in the same object, and the canonical review.verdict field that every other cited input uses carries the false value for v7 alone. The SHOULD-FIX is that OBL-R10-R6-INPUT-CORPUS.reason still rests on 'permission leftover-join.v7 measured OBL-R10-R6-INPUT-CORPUS leftoverDesign false on DR-105' while the same document declares v7 frozen, not current, and not recordable; three parallel sentences were moved to v9 and this fourth was missed. Both repairs are text-only, both are single-location, and neither moves a leftoverDesign value, since v9 measures that obligation false as well. DR-G09 stays OPEN, required-now stays 28, DR-105 is not SATISFIED, DR-114 leftover is not taken, OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains leftover-design, and nothing is sealed, recorded, or authorized by this verdict.
